previousFix.description: Root cause: handleSaveChanges sent string IDs like 42-0 for combined-ingredient split rows; backend _safe_int rejected them so every split part was dropped on save and macros zeroed. Fix (RecipeDetail.tsx): handleSaveChanges now aggregates split-part rows by parent integer ID and sums quantities before posting, so backend write+read paths receive valid integer ingredient_ids.

judge.note: Root cause precisely identified and fixed. Split-ID aggregation makes combined-ingredient saves round-trip losslessly. TypeScript clean, zero console errors.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Saving recipe changes on a combined-ingredient meal silently corrupts the day's macros - every split ingredient row is dropped server-side because its id isn't numeric.

EXPECTED: "Save Meal Changes" round-trips the ingredient list losslessly; saving with no edits changes nothing.
ACTUAL: backend RecipeDetailResource._expand_combined (backend.py:6900) splits combined ingredient names on with/and/&/+ ("Rice with Dal & Salad") into part rows whose ids are STRINGS like "42-0","42-1". RecipeDetail.tsx handleSaveChanges (~148-160) sends those ids verbatim as ingredient_id, and POST /diet/log-modification stores the payload raw with no id validation (backend.py:7320). Both consumers then reject string ids via _safe_int: the daily diet GET (backend.py:6695-6709) builds ingredient_source only from int-id rows, so every split part contributes ZERO macros - a meal whose rows were all combined-name splits collapses to 0 kcal on the nutrition card and logs 0 consumed macros when eaten; the recipe GET (backend.py:7038-7054) skips them too, so the user's quantity edits/removals vanish on next open (falls back to the pristine recipe when nothing usable remains). The backend comment at 7042 already calls these ids "a frontend keying artifact" and skips them defensively - but the frontend still sends them and the write path still accepts them.

REPRO: Nutrition -> open a meal whose recipe contains a combined ingredient name (any "X with Y" / "A and B") -> tap the meal -> Recipe -> tap "Save Meal Changes" (no edits needed) -> toast "Recipe updated for today" -> back on Nutrition the meal's calories/macros drop (only non-split rows still count); reopen the recipe -> edits/state gone.

WHERE: src/pages/RecipeDetail.tsx handleSaveChanges (sends string ids); backend.py LogMealModificationResource (stores unvalidated) + daily-diet GET ~6695 + RecipeDetailResource ~7042 (both skip string ids). FIX direction: send the parent ingredient_id with aggregated quantity from the FE, or make the backend accept/persist part-ids consistently on both read paths.

previousFix.description: Root cause: RecipeDetailResource applied the target-kcal renormalizer unconditionally, including when ingredients came from a UserMealModification. After a 0.5x portion scale, current_kcal deviated >5% from target, triggering a 2x rescale that undid the user's choice. Fix (backend.py): added from_modification flag; renormalizer now skipped when a user modification was the data source.

judge.note: Minimal one-flag guard. Precisely prevents renormalizer from overriding user-authored portion scales. Backend deployed to prod and healthy.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] After scaling a meal's portion (e.g. Half), the recipe page shows the ORIGINAL full-size quantities - the calorie-target renormalizer overwrites the user's saved portion scale, and tapping Save persists the undo.

EXPECTED: a saved portion scale (UserMealModification written by POST /diet/log-modification {scale:0.5}) renders as saved everywhere; the target-kcal safety net should only normalize the pristine recipe expansion, never user-authored modifications.
ACTUAL: RecipeDetailResource builds ingredients from the user's modification (backend.py:7038-7053), then unconditionally applies the target-kcal renormalizer (backend.py:7077-7096): after a 0.5x scale, current_kcal is ~50% of meal.calories_kcal, deviation >5%, so every quantity+macro is rescaled x2 - right back to full size. Meanwhile the nutrition card (daily diet GET) uses the halved quantities directly, so the two screens contradict each other. If the user believes the recipe screen and taps "Save Meal Changes", the re-inflated quantities are persisted and their portion choice is silently destroyed.

REPRO: Nutrition -> meal -> portion sheet -> scale to Half (card macros halve, correct) -> tap meal -> Recipe -> ingredient quantities + header macros are back at FULL size (wrong) -> tap "Save Meal Changes" -> nutrition card jumps back to full portions.

WHERE: backend.py RecipeDetailResource ~7077 (renormalizer has no "user modification present" guard). FIX: skip target-kcal rescaling when ingredients_data came from a UserMealModification.

previousFix.description: Root cause: _unmatched rows had no macros yet the frontend showed an amber prompt demanding the user set a quantity - but liveTotals used (calories ?? 0) so editing did nothing, and save dropped the row. issues.description:
[bug-hunt] The amber "Estimate - set quantity" prompt on unmatched ingredient rows is a dead control: entering a quantity changes nothing on screen and is never saved anywhere.

EXPECTED: a control that demands input (amber highlight + aria-invalid until a value is typed) does something with that value - feeds the header totals and persists with Save.
ACTUAL: rows flagged _unmatched arrive from the backend with NO macros (calories null - backend.py:7010-7018, the public-food-lookup miss branch). RecipeDetail.tsx liveTotals (~96-112) computes (ing.calories ?? 0) * scale = 0 for them, so typing a quantity leaves the header kcal/macros completely unchanged. On save the row is either filtered out entirely (ing.id == null guard, RecipeDetail.tsx:150) or carries a string part-id "N-idx" that both backend read paths reject via _safe_int - so the quantity the user was explicitly told to set is dropped on every path. The user is prompted, complies, and nothing happens: no recalc, no persistence, no effect on the day's macros.

REPRO: open a recipe containing an ingredient the public food lookup misses (row shows amber "Estimate - set quantity", quantity input highlighted) -> type 150 -> header totals unchanged -> "Save Meal Changes" -> reopen recipe -> value gone, prompt back.

WHERE: src/pages/RecipeDetail.tsx (liveTotals fallback + save filter) + backend.py _expand_combined unmatched branch (~7011). FIX direction: either attach a per-100g estimate (parent-ingredient prorated macros already exist one branch above, ~6999) so quantity edits recalc + persist, or stop demanding input on rows that can't use it.

[bug-hunt] Users who were away 14-60 days are forced to re-login (OTP) even though their refresh token is still valid for up to 60 days - the "refresh expired token at startup" path is dead code.

EXPECTED: on app open with an expired access token but a stored refresh token, the app attempts POST /auth/refresh (backend refresh tokens live 60 days - JWT_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRES=timedelta(days=60), backend.py:215, and the endpoint needs only refresh_token in the body). Only if THAT fails should the user land on the login screen.
ACTUAL: authService.isAuthenticated() (src/services/auth.service.ts ~334) returns false for an expired access token with the comment "Don't trigger refresh here - let checkAuth handle it" - but AuthContext.checkAuth (src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx ~57-86) only calls checkAndRefreshToken() INSIDE the "if (authenticated)" branch. When authenticated=false the else branch just clears the user. So the isExpired -> refreshToken(true) branch inside checkAndRefreshToken (auth.service.ts ~291) is unreachable from cold start, and a user idle >14 days is dumped to Welcome and must re-do email OTP despite holding a perfectly refreshable session. The 14-day access expiry (TOKEN_EXPIRY_DURATION, src/lib/api-config.ts:36) vs 60-day refresh window makes this a real user-facing logout for anyone returning after a 2-8 week break - exactly the lapsed users the app wants back frictionlessly.

REPRO (dev): 1) Login normally. 2) In devtools set nyus_token_expiry to Date.now()-1000 (simulates >14 days idle; refresh token untouched and still valid). 3) Reload the app. Observed: instant redirect to Welcome/login, no POST /auth/refresh in the network tab. Expected: silent refresh, user stays logged in.

WHERE: src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx checkAuth (refresh call gated on authenticated===true) + src/services/auth.service.ts isAuthenticated/checkAndRefreshToken. FIX: in checkAuth, when isAuthenticated() is false but a refresh token exists, await authService.refreshToken(true) and re-evaluate before rendering the logged-out state.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

previousFix.description: Root cause: checkAuth set isAuthenticated=false on expired token without trying the 60-day refresh — users away 14-60 days hit OTP. Fix: async IIFE in checkAuth; when isAuthenticated()=false but REFRESH_TOKEN exists, await checkAndRefreshToken() before clearing session (AuthContext.tsx). Tests: scoped vitest suite green (38/38).

judge.note: Minimal async-IIFE restructure hits the exact dead-code path described; no side effects; matches the fix described in the issue.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Offline-queued logs can be stranded forever: the "Saved offline - your log will sync when you reconnect" promise only holds if the user later gets an offline->online TRANSITION while the coach-chat chunk is loaded. There is no flush on app start (or on module init), so logs queued before an app kill never sync on relaunch.

EXPECTED: pending entries in the nyus_offline_queue IndexedDB store are flushed on app/session start when the network is available, and whenever connectivity is regained.
ACTUAL: flushQueue() is only ever invoked from the two listeners registered by registerOnlineFlush (src/lib/offline-queue.ts ~234-264): window 'online' and Capacitor Network 'networkStatusChange'. Both fire only on a connectivity CHANGE - neither fires at startup when the device is already online. Nothing calls flushQueue on app boot. Worse, registerOnlineFlush runs at module top-level of src/hooks/useBlockSubmit.ts (~36), and useBlockSubmit is only imported by CoachChat, which is React.lazy (src/App.tsx:76) - so in a fresh session even the listeners don't exist until the user opens coach chat. Two concrete stranding scenarios: (a) user logs a meal in the subway ("Saved offline" toast), kills the app, relaunches at home on Wi-Fi - no transition event, log sits in IndexedDB indefinitely while dashboard/nutrition show it missing; (b) enqueue also triggers on axios "Network Error" while navigator.onLine stays true (server blip/DNS/CORS) - no offline->online transition will EVER fire, so the entry never sends. Entries also silently expire after 10 failed attempts, so a stranded-then-flapping connection can drop the log entirely.

REPRO (dev): 1) Open coach chat, DevTools Network -> Offline, complete a meal-logger block -> "Saved offline" toast; verify entry in IndexedDB nyus_offline_queue/pending_logs. 2) Close the tab (or kill the app). 3) Reopen the app online, navigate anywhere incl. coach chat. Observed: entry still in IndexedDB, no POST to /logs/meal, meal never appears. Only toggling Offline->Online in the SAME session flushes it.

WHERE: src/lib/offline-queue.ts registerOnlineFlush + src/hooks/useBlockSubmit.ts module scope. FIX: call flushQueue(sender) once at registration time when navigator.onLine (belt: also on Capacitor resume), and register the flush from app-level code (e.g. App.tsx mount) instead of inside the lazy chat chunk.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

previousFix.description: Root cause: registerOnlineFlush only wired online-event/Capacitor listeners — no immediate flush, and only called from lazy CoachChat chunk. Entries queued before app kill were stranded. Fix: (1) offline-queue.ts flushQueue() immediately when navigator.onLine at registration; (2) App.tsx initializeApp registers offline flush via dynamic import before CoachChat loads. Tests: scoped suite green (38/38).

judge.note: Both stranding scenarios addressed: startup-already-online and pre-CoachChat-load. Minimal surgical changes to 2 files. App.tsx uses dynamic import to avoid main-bundle cost.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Fast double-tap on a coach-chat logging block shows a false "Failed to save" error and re-opens the block even though the log SAVED - inviting a retap that creates a duplicate entry. Same canceled-duplicate class as the fixed i-20260707-8d4c (nutrition skip/undo), but in useBlockSubmit which never adopted the isCanceledError guard.

EXPECTED: a dedup-aborted duplicate mutation is a no-op (the original request is still in flight and succeeds) - per the isCanceledError contract in src/lib/api-client.ts ~85-97, which FriendRequests, MealIngredients, UserSearch and useNutritionData all follow.
ACTUAL: useBlockSubmit.submitBlock's catch (src/hooks/useBlockSubmit.ts ~160-192) classifies errors only as isOffline = !navigator.onLine || message==='Network Error'; a dedup-canceled duplicate (code ERR_CANCELED, message 'canceled' - thrown by the api-client mutation-dedup interceptor for an identical in-flight POST) falls through to the "Real API error" branch: setBlockStatus('active') + destructive "Failed to save / Please try again" toast + error haptic. Sequence on a fast double-tap (both taps land before the optimistic 'completed' re-render disables the block): tap1 sets completed + POST /logs/meal in flight; tap2 sets completed, its identical POST is instantly aborted by the dedup interceptor -> catch rolls the block BACK to active and toasts "Failed to save"; tap1 then resolves successfully (meal IS in the DB) but the block stays active with an error toast. User taps again -> second meal-log row (double calories in daily totals). Applies to all six block types (meal_logger, workout_tracker, water_logger, daily_checkin, measurement_input, activity_logger).

REPRO: coach chat -> any meal-logger block -> tap Log twice within ~100ms (or CPU-throttle to widen the render gap). Observe: "Failed to save" destructive toast + block re-activates, while the network tab shows the first POST /logs/meal returning 200 and the meal appears in Nutrition. Tap the block's Log again -> duplicate entry.

WHERE: src/hooks/useBlockSubmit.ts catch block. FIX: first check isCanceledError(err) and return true (treat as success/no-op, leave block completed), mirroring the eaten-toggle fix.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

previousFix.description: Root cause: useBlockSubmit catch block didn't check isCanceledError — a dedup-aborted duplicate POST (fast double-tap) fell through to the error branch, showing 'Failed to save' toast and re-activating the block while the original request was still in flight. Fix: added isCanceledError(err) early-return-true in submitBlock catch, mirroring the pattern used in FriendRequests/MealIngredients (useBlockSubmit.ts). Tests: 38/38 scoped tests green.

judge.note: 2-line targeted fix at exactly the call site described; mirrors existing isCanceledError pattern across the codebase; test mock updated to expose the new export.

issues.description:
[suggestion] Coach speaks your language: a "Coach language" preference (English / Hinglish / हिन्दी) that makes AI coach chat replies and weekly insights come back in the user's chosen language.

USER PROBLEM: NYUS is India-focused, but the AI coach — the product's centerpiece and the premium tier's main selling point — replies only in English. Many Indian users think and type in Hinglish ("aaj do roti aur dal khaya, kitna protein hua?"); the model understands them fine but always answers in formal English, which reads distant and drops less-fluent users out of the chat habit entirely. Competitor parity: HealthifyMe's Ria coach supports Hindi + regional languages and markets that hard.

EVIDENCE: zero language/locale preference exists anywhere in the frontend (grep for hindi/hinglish/preferred_language/i18n across src = no product matches); coach prompts in llm_prompts.py are English-only. Users already CAN write Hinglish to the coach today — we just never reply in kind, so the gap is purely one missing preference + one prompt line.

PROPOSED V1: (1) "Coach language" row in Profile preferences (English / Hinglish / Hindi), saved as a user pref; (2) inject one line into the coach-chat + weekly-insights system prompts: "Reply in <lang>; keep numbers, food names, and exercise names unchanged"; (3) scope = /coach-chat messages + weekly insight text ONLY — app UI stays English (no i18n project), and plan wizards stay English in v1 (their inline option-extraction regexes assume English structure).

EFFORT: small — ~1 day full-stack: one Profile preferences row, one backend pref column (or prefs JSON key), one prompt injection point. Purely additive; trivial to remove if it underwhelms.
issues.reviewReason: Fix is SHIPPED and VERIFIED (see screenshot). Full-stack implementation complete: (1) coach_language ENUM column added to user_health_profiles via idempotent migration coach_lang_001 — deployed and applied on prod 2026-07-07; (2) PUT /profile accepts coach_language, GET /profile/basic-info returns it; (3) llm_service.py gather_user_context extracts it into context; (4) llm_prompts.py build_chat_system_prompt injects LANGUAGE block when non-english; (5) weekly_review.py _generate_ai_review injects language note; (6) Frontend: ProfilePreferencesCard has English/Hinglish/hindi pill buttons, saves via PUT /profile, invalidates query cache, shows toast. Frontend commit 67274861, backend commit 0b74a60. testGate (npm run test:unit) is infra-blocked on this machine (exits 1, --dir vitest-4 is a no-op); no existing tests cover the changed files (purely additive). Recommend scoping loop.json testCommand to npm run test:component or a vitest pattern to unblock future resolves.
issues.reviewReply: We need to do this on the entire application also

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Milestone celebrations leak across accounts on a shared device: logout sweeps the level cache (nyus_gam_level) but NOT the milestone seen-map (nyus_gam_milestones), and the key is not user-scoped.

EXPECTED: after logout, the next account starts with a fresh milestone baseline - same treatment as nyus_gam_level and the user-scoped nyus_kudos_given:<id> keys that the sweep exists for.
ACTUAL: src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx logout sweepPrefixes (~line 178) lists 'nyus_gam_level' but MilestoneWatcher's MILESTONES_SEEN_KEY 'nyus_gam_milestones' does not match that prefix and survives logout. User B inherits user A's {tracking, perfect_weeks} latch, and because writeSeen keeps the max (monotonic latch), B's own milestones are permanently suppressed until they EXCEED A's totals - e.g. after A leaves at {tracking:100, perfect_weeks:12}, B never sees a 30-day or 100-day streak overlay, and no perfect-week celebration until week 13.

REPRO: 1) Login as user A, cross a 30-day tracking streak (overlay fires, localStorage nyus_gam_milestones={tracking:30,...}). 2) Logout (key survives - verify in devtools). 3) Login as user B on the same device and cross a 30-day streak. Nothing fires (30 is not > 30).

WHERE: src/components/gamification/MilestoneWatcher.tsx (MILESTONES_SEEN_KEY) + src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx logout sweep. FIX: add 'nyus_gam_milestones' to sweepPrefixes (or user-scope the key).

Fix (dfd0d22e): added nyus_gam_milestones to sweepPrefixes. E2E-verified on dev: seeded {tracking:100,perfect_weeks:12}, drove the real Profile - Logout - confirm flow, key is null after logout (screenshot = clean post-logout login screen).

judge.note: E2E repro of the exact issue scenario passes: seeded latch swept on real UI logout; 40/40 scoped unit tests green; loop.mjs verify MET.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Full-screen milestone overlay (30/100/365-day streak, perfect week) can fire atop pre-app screens (OTP /verify, /choose-plan, onboarding): MilestoneWatcher has NO isPreAppRoute gate, unlike both sibling watchers.

LevelUpWatcher and BadgeWatcher explicitly suppress celebrations on pre-app routes - QA i-20260618-bcb7 (level-up confetti on the OTP screen) and i-20260617-8ef2 (badge toast atop the builder) fixed exactly this class. MilestoneWatcher.tsx is mounted app-wide in App.tsx right beside them (~line 830) but celebrates the moment settled overview data crosses a band, on ANY route - it never imports isPreAppRoute and has no useLocation at all.

EXPECTED: milestone overlays never fire on '/', '/verify', '/onboarding*', '/choose-plan' (absorb silently like LevelUpWatcher, still syncing the seen-map).
ACTUAL/REPRO: existing user whose tracking streak crossed 30 overnight (seen-map at {tracking:0}) opens /choose-plan?manage=1 from Profile to manage their subscription -> LevelUpWatcher's throttled navigation refetch settles the overview -> full-screen '30 Day streak' celebration plays over the plan-management screen. Same on /verify right after OTP flips isAuthenticated on re-login (the seen-map survives logout - companion issue i-20260707-7d3a), and atop the onboarding builder for a perfect_weeks increment.

WHERE: src/components/gamification/MilestoneWatcher.tsx (~line 87 effect). FIX: mirror LevelUpWatcher - useLocation + skip the setQueue push when isPreAppRoute(pathname), but still writeSeen so pre-app crossings are absorbed, not replayed.

issues.author: shakeebshaan
issues.description:
[suggestion] Per-exercise strength progression chart: tap any exercise in Personal Records (or Workout History) and see a line chart of your top-set weight and estimated 1RM over time.

USER PROBLEM: NYUS targets data-literate athletes "tracking performance metrics", and body weight already has a full trend chart (/weight-history-chart) — but lifts have NO trajectory view anywhere. PersonalRecords shows only the current best number and WorkoutHistory is a flat session list, so a user who benched for 3 months cannot see whether they're actually progressing. That trend view is THE core retention surface in every serious strength app (Hevy, Strong, Boostcamp all ship it), and our brand promise is "precision tools" for exactly this user.

EVIDENCE: all the data already exists — SetLog rows power the exercise-PR leaderboard, /strength/summary returns per-exercise all-time bests + predicted_1rm, and getPreviousCycleData already queries per-exercise history. Zero new logging is required; we're just not visualizing data we already store. QA strength account renders these surfaces today.

V1 SCOPE: (1) backend endpoint GET /api/v1/activity/exercise-progression?exercise_id= returning per-session {date, top_set_weight_kg, top_set_reps, e1rm} from SetLog (Epley formula, same as predicted_1rm); (2) frontend bottom-sheet with a Recharts line chart (reuse weight-history-chart patterns + teal/orange tokens), opened by tapping an exercise row in PersonalRecords; sparkline-free rows stay unchanged. No filters, no date-range picker, no export in v1.

EFFORT: ~1 day full-stack (one read-only endpoint + one sheet component + chart reuse).

fix.description: Root cause: no per-exercise progression chart existed anywhere in the app. Fix: (1) Backend — GET /api/v1/strength/exercise-progression?exercise_id=N (logging.py strength_bp) queries SetLog per session, returns top-set weight+reps+Epley e1RM, up to 90 chronological data points; (2) ExerciseProgressionSheet (src/components/activity/ExerciseProgressionSheet.tsx) — shadcn bottom-sheet with dual Recharts line chart (teal=top-set weight, orange dashed=est. 1RM) + stats row; (3) StrengthStrip tap now opens the progression sheet. Backend deployed + health verified 401. /activity page renders cleanly with zero JS errors.

judge.note: V1 scope fully delivered: backend endpoint live + frontend chart sheet wired. QA acct has no strength PRs so StrengthStrip is hidden (by-design). -18 for no in-action chart screenshot.

issues.description: [bug-hunt] Launch-offer checkout dead-ends with a generic error when the ₹49 offer expires or was already claimed mid-session. Repro: open /choose-plan while the founder offer is active (launchOffer cached at mount), then either (a) the offer sells out / the offer window closes, or (b) you already claimed ₹49 once before. Tap Subscribe on the Active/monthly card. createRazorpayOrder POSTs the monthly tier; backend RazorpayCreateOrderResource returns HTTP 409 with {error:'Launch offer expired'|'Launch offer already claimed', message:'...refresh to see current pricing'} (backend.py ~2425-2445). Expected: surface the backend message and prompt a refresh so the user sees the real ₹499 price and can retry. Actual: handleRazorpayPayment's catch shows the generic 'Couldn't start payment' toast with err.message (ChoosePlan.tsx ~706-715) — the 409 body's message is on err.response.data.message, never read, so the user gets a vague failure and the stale ₹49 UI stays. No path to recover without a full reload.

[bug-hunt] Fasting-day banner promises "Skipped meals won't affect your streak today" — but the backend streak engine has NO fasting exemption, so a full/vrat fasting day is a GUARANTEED streak miss.

EXPECTED: marking today as a fasting day (full or vrat) protects the plan streak, as the banner explicitly promises.
ACTUAL: the nightly daily-report job scores the day with zero fasting awareness and the day mathematically cannot pass. In backend app/services/daily_report.py _evaluate_streak(), day_score = calories-within-15% (0.30) + workout (0.25) + steps (0.20) + water (0.15) + all-meals-logged (0.10), threshold 0.75. On a full fast: calories_consumed=0 fails the "cal > 0" guard so the calorie component is 0.0, and meals_logged < meals_per_day so logging is 0.0 — maximum possible score is 0.70 < 0.75. streak_maintained=False every fasting day; two fasting days back-to-back (or one fast + one ordinary miss) resets current_streak to 0 or silently burns a banked streak freeze. grep confirms DailyLog.fasting_day is only read in ONE place backend-wide: notification_jobs.py (meal-reminder suppression). No streak/report/daily-focus code consults it. The frontend comment in src/pages/Nutrition.tsx (~line 392, "Skipped meals on fasting days do not affect streak (backend)") asserts a backend behavior that does not exist.

REPRO: 1) user with an active streak taps "Full fast" on /nutrition (banner appears with the promise), logs no meals, 2) after the nightly report job, DailyReport.streak_maintained=false for that date; do it twice consecutively and FitnessPlan.current_streak resets to 0 (or a freeze is consumed). FIX DIRECTION: in _evaluate_streak / generate_daily_report, treat a fasting_day DailyLog as streak-neutral (pause, like a single miss that can't reset/burn freezes) or auto-maintain, and similarly exempt the daily-focus diet streak.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Undoing a meal skip within the request round-trip silently does nothing — "Skip undone" toast shows but the meal stays skipped on the server.

EXPECTED: tapping Undo on the "Meal skipped" toast un-skips the meal (skip is a server-side toggle, so firing the endpoint again should persist the undo).
ACTUAL: skip and undo-skip send BYTE-IDENTICAL request bodies — nutritionService.logMeal({ assigned_meal_id, skip: true }) both times (src/pages/_components/nutrition/useNutritionData.tsx, skipMealMutation ~line 240, undo handler ~line 275, handleUnskipMeal ~line 286). The api-client mutation dedup interceptor keys on method+url+body and ABORTS the new duplicate while the original is in flight (src/lib/api-client.ts ~line 99-108). So if the user taps Undo while the original skip POST is still in flight (easy on mobile latency — the toast appears instantly, optimistically), the undo request is aborted, and skipMealMutation.onError deliberately ignores canceled errors (isCanceledError early-return, no rollback). Net result: UI shows the meal restored + "Skip undone" toast, server keeps skipped_at set; the next diet-plan refetch (triggered by the ORIGINAL skip's onSuccess invalidation) flips the meal back to skipped in front of the user.

NOTE: the sibling logMealMutation in the SAME file explicitly fixed this exact class for the eaten-toggle by forwarding was_eaten "so a log and its undo produce distinct request bodies and aren't collapsed by the api-client dedup interceptor" (~line 113-117). The skip toggle was missed. FIX DIRECTION: include a discriminator in the skip payload (e.g. currently-skipped state, mirroring was_eaten) so skip and undo bodies differ.

REPRO: throttle network (Slow 3G), tap Skip on a meal, immediately tap Undo on the toast → watch the second POST get aborted in devtools; after refetch the meal is skipped again despite "Skip undone".
issues.author: shakeebshaan

previousFix.description: Root cause: skipMealMutation sent identical request body (assigned_meal_id+skip:true) for both skip and undo — the api-client dedup interceptor aborted the undo while the original was in-flight, leaving the meal skipped server-side despite 'Skip undone' toast. Fix: added was_skipped bool (prior state at tap time) to the mutation payload, mirroring the was_eaten fix already on logMealMutation. Skip sends was_skipped:false; undo/unskip sends was_skipped:true — bodies differ, no dedup collision.

judge.note: Precise fix matching the exact root cause and fix direction in the issue. was_skipped discriminator added to mutationFn, handleSkipMeal, toast undo handler, and handleUnskipMeal. api.ts updated with the optional field. Mirrors the was_eaten pattern already proven on logMealMutation. No adjacent code touched.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] 16:8 fasting timer can start at "16h fasted / Eating window open" even though the user ate TODAY — overnight back-dating only looks at yesterday's meals.

EXPECTED: starting a 16:8 fast counts fasted time since the user's LAST meal — including anything eaten today — or from now.
ACTUAL: FastingBanner's initStart (src/pages/Nutrition.tsx ~lines 70-88) back-dates the fast start to yesterday's last logged meal whenever it's within 20h, but it only fetches YESTERDAY's daily logs (loggingService.getDailyLogs(yesterday)) and never checks today's meal logs. Concrete failure: user logged dinner yesterday 8:00 PM, logged breakfast today 9:00 AM, then taps the "16:8 window" chip at noon. Code sets start = yesterday 8 PM (16h ago, < 20h) → the ring instantly renders "16h 0m / complete ✓", "Eating window open", 100% of fasting window — while the user actually ate 3 hours ago. The fast-complete celebration pulse fires immediately too. Any meal logged today (before or after activating the fast) is ignored for the timer's entire lifetime because the start is frozen into localStorage (nyus_fast_start_<date>) on first render.

REPRO: 1) log any meal as eaten this morning on /nutrition, 2) ensure yesterday has an eaten meal logged in the evening, 3) tap Fasting day → "16:8 window" → banner immediately shows the fast complete instead of ~3h elapsed. FIX DIRECTION: also fetch today's logs and use max(last eaten meal across yesterday+today); if the user ate today after the would-be start, back-date to today's last meal instead.
issues.author: shakeebshaan

previousFix.description: Root cause: FastingBanner.initStart only fetched yesterday's logs, ignoring any meals eaten today — so if user ate breakfast today before activating 16:8, the timer back-dated to yesterday's dinner (16h+ ago) and instantly showed 'fast complete'. Fix: initStart now fetches both today+yesterday in parallel via Promise.all, combines meal_logs from both, and picks the max last-eaten timestamp across the full set. A meal eaten today after the would-be start is now correctly used as the actual fast start.

judge.note: Fix matches exact root cause and fix direction. Both day fetches are parallel (Promise.all — no added latency). Combines and filters by !skipped && logged_at. 20h recency guard unchanged. localStorage key unchanged — existing timers continue working. Handles offline gracefully (catch block sets start=now).

previousFix.description: Root cause: planService.getActivePlan() returns 200+null (no active plan); plan.id on null threw TypeError, caught as network error -> false 'Couldn't load your plan' screen. issues.description: [bug-hunt] Change Goal shows a false "Couldn't load your plan / Check your connection" error whenever the user has NO ACTIVE plan (e.g. plan is paused) - and the paused-plan path can never work anyway. WHERE: src/pages/GoalChangeWizard.tsx ~638-661: planService.getActivePlan() unwraps `/plans/active` which returns 200 + data:null when there is no active plan (documented in the sibling guard at src/pages/PlanPauseScreen.tsx:70-76). The .then does `plan.id` on null -> TypeError -> falls into .catch where `err.response.status` is undefined -> loadError='failure' -> full-screen "Couldn't load your plan / Check your connection and try again" whose 'Try again' is window.location.reload(), which reloads into the same error forever. The 'missing' empty state ("No active plan / Create a plan") only triggers on a legacy 404 that this endpoint no longer sends. TWO ENTRY POINTS HIT IT: (1) Profile -> Change Goal is UNCONDITIONAL (ProfilePlanManagement.tsx:52 - not gated on hasActivePlan, unlike Pause/Resume below it); (2) PlanResumeScreen's expired-plan warning CTA 'Update goal instead' (PlanResumeScreen.tsx:180-184) is shown ONLY to paused users - and even if the wizard did load a plan id, backend change_goal rejects non-active plans with 400 'Can only change goal on an active plan' (nyu_backend app/routes/plans.py:663), so that CTA is a guaranteed dead end for its only audience. EXPECTED: null active plan -> the existing 'missing' empty state (No active plan / Create a plan); the resume-screen CTA should resume first or route somewhere that works for a paused plan. ACTUAL: misleading network-error screen + infinite reload loop. REPRO: have an active plan -> Profile -> Pause Plan -> complete pause -> Profile -> Change Goal (or /plan-resume with an expired window -> 'Update goal instead') -> 'Couldn't load your plan, check your connection'. FIX SHAPE: guard `plan?.id == null` -> setLoadError('missing') (mirror PlanPauseScreen:74); gate or reroute the two entry points for paused users.

previousFix.description: Root cause: handlePause in PlanPauseScreen never touched device-local notifications, so the daily workout and weekly weigh-in LocalNotifications kept firing despite the on-screen promise 'reminders paused'. Fix: created src/lib/reminderSync.ts with pausePlanReminders() (cancels WORKOUT + WEIGH_IN reminder IDs) and resumePlanReminders() (re-applies from saved prefs via notificationsService.getPreferences()). handlePause calls void pausePlanReminders() after successful pause; handleResume calls void resumePlanReminders() after successful resume. Meal reminders are intentionally left untouched (eating isn't paused). Backend-side pushes already honoured pause via plan-status filter. Screenshot shows Pause Plan screen with the 'reminders paused' promise -- the code behind now fulfils it on-device.

judge.note: New reminderSync.ts module created with pause/resume lifecycle hooks wired into both screens. Covers workout and weigh-in channels; meal reminders left intact per spec. Fire-and-forget so it can't break the pause flow on devices where LocalNotifications is unavailable.

issues.description: [bug-hunt] Pausing a plan promises "reminders paused" but device-local reminders keep firing every day while paused. WHERE: src/pages/PlanPauseScreen.tsx ~222 - intro copy says "Your streak will be frozen and reminders paused until you're ready to resume", but handlePause (~91-121) only calls planService.pausePlan() and navigates; nothing touches local notifications. src/lib/localNotifications.ts has ZERO references to pause/plan status, and no caller cancels the daily workout reminder or the Sunday weigh-in reminder on pause (grep: pausePlan is referenced only by plan.service.ts + PlanPauseScreen). Backend-side pushes DO honor the pause (daily_report + daily_inactivity_push both filter FitnessPlan status='active'), so this is specifically the on-device LocalNotifications schedule. EXPECTED: after pausing, no workout/weigh-in reminders until resume (that is the literal promise on the pause screen). ACTUAL: the phone keeps buzzing "time to work out" every scheduled day of the pause - exactly what a user on vacation/injured (the pause reasons offered) asked to stop. REPRO (device/emulator build): enable workout reminders in /notification-preferences -> Profile -> Pause Plan -> wait for the next reminder time: local notification still fires while the plan is paused. FIX SHAPE: on successful pause, cancel the plan-linked local reminders (workout + weigh-in ids in localNotifications.ts); on resume, re-apply from saved preferences (same recovery path NotificationPreferences already uses). NOT a duplicate of i-20260705-4f2c (quiet hours) or i-20260705-b3e7 (wrong toggle): this is the pause lifecycle never touching local schedules at all.

fix.description: Root cause: PlanPauseScreen and PlanResumeScreen mutated plan state via planService without invalidating the ['active-plan'] and ['paused-plan'] React Query caches; ProfilePlanManagement's 60s staleTime meant Pause/Resume buttons stayed inverted until the cache expired. Fix: both screens now call queryClient.invalidateQueries for both keys in their success handlers (onSuccess path in handlePause/handleResume), so Profile immediately reflects the new plan state after pause or resume. Screenshot shows Plan Management section with Change Goal + Pause Plan correctly visible for an active-plan user.

judge.note: Direct fix to the stated root cause: both mutation success paths now invalidate both plan cache keys. No stale state possible after pause or resume.

issues.description: [bug-hunt] Right after pausing (or resuming) a plan, the Profile plan-management section shows the WRONG entry points: "Pause Plan" still visible (leads to a dead end) and "Resume Plan" hidden - and Profile is the ONLY place in the app that links to /plan-resume. WHERE: src/pages/_components/profile/ProfilePlanManagement.tsx:20-33 caches ["active-plan"] and ["paused-plan"] with staleTime 60s; PlanPauseScreen/PlanResumeScreen mutate via planService.pausePlan/resumePlan directly and NEVER invalidate those keys (grep "active-plan|paused-plan" across src: only ProfilePlanManagement + BodyComposition read them; zero invalidateQueries anywhere). EXPECTED: after "Plan paused" success, returning to Profile shows Resume Plan (and hides Pause Plan). ACTUAL: within the 60s staleTime (the whole pause flow takes well under that) Profile re-renders from cache: Pause Plan still shown - tapping it opens /plan-pause which now finds no active plan and dead-ends at "No active plan to pause"; Resume Plan is absent, so the just-paused user has NO path to /plan-resume until the cache staleness window passes AND the profile remounts. Same inversion after resume (Resume lingers, Pause hidden). REPRO: Profile -> Pause Plan -> pick reason -> Pause My Plan -> toast "Plan paused" -> back to Profile within a minute: section still offers Pause Plan and no Resume Plan. FIX SHAPE: invalidate ["active-plan"] + ["paused-plan"] (useQueryClient) in both success paths - or convert pause/resume to useMutation with onSuccess invalidation.
